target_customer: Cultivated meat producers (early) and later biopharma, diagnostics, food and agriculture firms that need hard-to-make recombinant proteins
problem: Growth factors and media are the largest cost of cell-cultured meat, so producers could not reach price parity; Future Fields aimed to make growth factors cheaply and animal-free.
business_model: B2B sale of growth factors and custom recombinant proteins (product and service revenue)
product_category: biotech inputs / recombinant protein expression for cellular agriculture

founders.name: Matt Anderson-Baron
education: University of Alberta, PhD in cell biology
founders.background_notes: YC page says he was one of the first Canadian grant recipients in cellular agriculture.

founders.name: Jalene Anderson-Baron
founders.background_notes: YC page says a decade of analytical roles on environmental and social causes, health and social research, project management and policy.

founders.name: Lejjy Gafour
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CEO in Crunchbase News 2021-02 coverage; not listed on the YC page.

competitors.what: animal-free growth factor developer named alongside Future Fields

technical_complexity.rationale: Producing bioactive recombinant growth factors at low cost and later building a fruit fly expression system requires real biology R&D beyond standard software or hardware engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary expression platform and know-how are hard to replicate, but growth factors are commodity-like and rivals plus microbial producers exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquired or neutralised the company in sources found; the market of cultivated meat stayed small.

market_need_then: GFI's 2020 data work (published 2021) identifies growth factors and recombinant proteins as the bulk of cultured meat media cost, and Bee Partners reportedly mapped about 60 cellular agriculture companies by 2021.

identity.mascot_or_character: Fruit fly imagery with a playful 'Flyer' nickname
identity.visual_style: Clean layout with fruit fly imagery
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, optimistic, mission-driven with light wordplay

branding.brand_signature: Fruit fly identity around the EntoEngine platform

brand_strength.rationale: Coherent fruit fly story after the pivot, but the generic name and little press about the brand itself were found.

pivots.to: low-cost growth factors for cultivated meat
pivots.why: Sources say the company moved from lab-grown meat to reducing the cost of growth factors; date approximate and reason not detailed

pivots.to: fruit fly based protein platform for biopharma, food and agriculture
pivots.why: Sources say it saw growth potential beyond cellular agriculture; exact date approximate

outcome_analysis: Future Fields joined YC in Summer 2020 with growth factors for cultured meat, raised a $2.2M seed led by Bee Partners in February 2021 and then widened its market to a fruit fly protein platform serving biopharma and agriculture. It is still active; later aggregator totals are inconsistent so the funding picture is incomplete and no exit is known.
notes: Competitor source (FoodNavigator, 2021-03) is about seven months after the Summer 2020 batch; only the snippet was seen, not the page. Unverified aggregator figures: sp-edge says USD 11.2M raised including Feb 2023 (Bee Partners, Toyota Ventures); CB Insights says $21.53M over 9 rounds with a Series A of $8M on 2025-06-17; another says a $480,000 pre-seed from angels and Grow Agrifood Tech Accelerator. None confirmed by a second outlet so not recorded as rounds. The $125,000 YC amount is stated by Crunchbase News as included in the seed total. Founding year listings range 2017 to 2019; YC says 2018. Pivot dates approximate. futurefields.io/about returned 404.
